reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the existence of κ as a design parameter and its link to multiple CPSs and improved strength-ductility synergy, but it does not provide evidence for simultaneous improvement of Young’s modulus or fracture resistance, nor does it quantify the predicted 5–20% improvements across all four properties.
premises: A parameter κ (ratio of short-range interplanar interactions) controls the formation of multiple close-packed stacking sequences (CPSs) in FCC HEAs.
Tuning κ to a near-degeneracy condition reduces activation barriers for generating stacking faults, twins, and HCP-like regions.
A higher density of diverse nanoscale CPSs enhances work hardening, improving both strength and ductility.
This κ-guided design can achieve simultaneous improvements in strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance over conventional CoCrNi-based HEAs.
